title: A killed test-launcher run stays "running" forever; give readers a liveness signal that survives PID reuse
outcome: A killed test-launcher run stays "running" forever; give readers a liveness signal that survives PID reuse
acceptance: A test kills a running launcher and shows its run reported as interrupted, and shows that a reused PID alone does not make it look alive
The launcher's own status or summary reports a run whose signal has gone stale as interrupted, not running

While a run executes, results.json carries a liveness signal that a reader can check without trusting the PID alone: a heartbeat the launcher refreshes on a timer even during a long stage, or the launcher process's start identity next to its PID
docs/development.md (test launcher) says how a reader tells running from interrupted

completion.summary: results.json now carries a heartbeat {at, everyMs} that the launcher refreshes on a timer, even during long stages; the default is 10 s and ENGRAM_LAUNCHER_HEARTBEAT_MS sets 1 to 600 s. A run without a terminal result is RUNNING while its heartbeat is at most 3 × everyMs old, and INTERRUPTED after that; the pid is never read. `summary` reports RUNNING, INTERRUPTED or UNKNOWN. A new test kills a real launcher and shows the run read as interrupted even while a live process holds the recorded pid. docs/development.md explains how to tell the states apart. Saves retry a briefly refused Windows rename. Landed as 3ed72d1 (pushed; scripts only, no install). TermAl has the contract for its liveness reader. Independent evaluation 886291bb passed all 4 criteria.
